seo.title: Heladerias in Buenos Aires (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the best heladerias in Buenos Aires for 2026 — curated picks with maps, hours, and insider tips.

hero.subtitle: Buenos Aires has the best ice cream outside of Italy — and locals will fight you on that. From 88-year-old artisanal institutions to Patagonian chocolate empires, here are the heladerías that Reddit and porteños actually recommend.

faq.question: What is the best heladería in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Cadore is the most famous — ranked in National Geographic's Top 10 worldwide. But locals are split between Cadore, Scannapieco (open since 1938), and Heladería Gruta (highest Google rating at 4.7★). For best all-around experience, start at Cadore and explore from there.

faq.question: What flavor should I try first in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Dulce de leche, without question. It's the Messi of Argentine ice cream flavors — every heladería has it, and it's the benchmark by which locals judge quality. After that, try sambayón (egg yolk and sweet wine) and chocolate amargo (bitter chocolate).

faq.question: Is Argentine ice cream the same as Italian gelato?
faq.answer: Yes and no. Buenos Aires' helado tradition was brought by Italian immigrants and uses similar techniques — fresh ingredients, lower fat content, and denser texture than American ice cream. But Argentine gelato has evolved its own identity, especially with flavors like dulce de leche and goat milk caramel.

faq.question: Can I get ice cream delivered in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Most heladerías deliver, many until 2-3 AM. Freddo and Persicco have the widest delivery coverage. You can order through PedidosYa or directly from the shops. There's usually a half-kilo minimum for delivery.

faq.question: How much does ice cream cost in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: A small cone (cono) with 2 flavors runs about ARS 2,000-4,000 ($2-4 USD). A quarter-kilo tub with 3 flavors is around ARS 4,000-8,000. Freddo and Lucciano's are on the pricier end; Pistacchio and local shops are more budget-friendly.

faq.question: What are the best neighborhoods for ice cream in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Palermo has the highest concentration (Tufic, Lucciano's), but don't sleep on Chacarita (Scannapieco, Occo), Belgrano (La Gruta), and Recoleta (Rapanui, Buffala). San Telmo and San Cristóbal have excellent options too.

faq.question: When is ice cream season in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Every season is ice cream season in Buenos Aires — porteños eat helado year-round. But summer (December-February) is peak season when lines form outside the most popular shops. For shorter waits, visit on weekday afternoons.
